# Convergent Evidence

An argument built from several independently weak signals that point the same way, rather than from
one decisive test. Each signal on its own has an innocent explanation; the claim is that the
conjunction does not. [[labour-fraud-analysis]] states the frame explicitly — "not a smoking gun, a
convergence", and "No single one proves intent".

## The signals

| Signal | Computation | Weakness taken alone |
|---|---|---|
| Bulk sponsorship | group permits by (day, employer); flag days above a threshold | a genuine large employer hires in batches |
| Shared identifiers | value-count concentration on contact fields | shared inboxes are common and legal |
| Wage uniformity | modal spike in a 30-bin histogram of contract values | a standard rate produces the same spike |
| Entity succession | permits migrating predecessor→successor across a year | ordinary corporate restructuring |
| Network bridging | people adjacent to two or more companies in an entity graph | people change jobs |

Each is reproduced identically in the narrative, the dashboard, the notebook and the tests — the
[[reproducible-analysis]] property that keeps the four surfaces from disagreeing.

## What the method is, precisely

Threshold flags, group-bys, value-count concentration, and a graph — then an argument. Stating that
plainly matters more than it might seem, because a reader who sees "forensic data analysis" will
assume a standard toolkit that **is not present here**:

- no Benford's law
- no z-score, IQR, or any statistical outlier detection
- no time-series anomaly model
- no significance testing of any kind
- no coefficient of variation or entropy behind the "uniformity" read — it is a visual modal spike
- no centrality measure; graph degree is used only for node sizing, and "bridging" is a neighbour count
- no ghost-employee test as such — the outsized payroll line and the implausible-age employees are
  narrative observations, not computed
- no duplicate-record detection as an analytic; the content-hash folding is an ingestion step, see
  [[chain-of-custody]]

None of that is a defect of the *argument*, which never claims statistical inference. It is a
correction to what a reader would otherwise assume.

## Convergence needs independence, and that is the soft spot

The signals are only mutually reinforcing if they are independent. Several are computed from the same
permit table, so a single upstream irregularity could produce more than one of them. Nothing in the
repo argues for independence. Compare [[dual-implementation-as-cross-check]], where independence is
the entire design goal.
